name: qara-view Phase 2 — Break the Import Cycle

stories.title: Extract the view context into its own module
stories.description: src/App.tsx currently owns ViewContextValue, ViewContext, and useView, while both components import useView back from '../App'. That is a real import cycle: neither component can be understood, moved, or tested without dragging in the app root. Move the context into its own module. Separately, ViewContext is created with null! which lies to the type system — a consumer rendered outside the provider gets a property-access crash on null instead of a diagnosable error.
acceptance_criteria: src/lib/view-context.ts exists and exports ViewContextValue, ViewContext, and useView
ViewContext is typed to admit null and is created with null as its real default value, not with a null! assertion
useView throws an Error whose message names the missing provider when the context is absent, rather than returning null
src/App.tsx no longer declares ViewContextValue, ViewContext, or useView, and imports ViewContext from src/lib/view-context.ts

stories.title: Repoint the components and prove the cycle is gone
stories.description: With the context extracted, SaveToolbar and InfoPanel must import useView from the new module rather than from the app root. The absence of the cycle is the acceptance condition, not a side effect — assert it directly.
acceptance_criteria: A new architecture check (e.g. scripts/check-architecture.ts) exits non-zero when any module under src/ other than src/main.tsx imports the application root, and exits 0 otherwise.
Proven RED before GREEN: with a temporary reverse import present the check exits non-zero; record that evidence, then revert the import.
package.json's `check` script runs the architecture check alongside lint, types, tests.
`bun run check` exits 0 on the clean tree.
`bun test` reports 31 pass / 0 fail with tests/persistence.test.ts and tests/server.test.ts unmodified.
